title: Celestial circles
caption: Star circles over the road to ALMA, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Stars trace circles around the southern celestial pole, which sits at the centre of this image. Above the pole float the Magellanic Clouds, Small and Large, a pair of Milky Way satellite galaxies that can only be seen from the southern hemisphere, showing as diffuse bluish clouds. On the left, a dense crowd of stars marks the centre of the Milky Way.

ESO Photo Ambassador Adhemar Duro took the picture after pulling over at the side of the road on his way to one of ESO's observing sites in Chile. That road climbs to the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), which sits at an altitude of 5000 metres.
The circles are a product of the long exposure. As Earth turns, every star appears to orbit the celestial pole, and while the shutter stays open, each one draws an arc of light.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure photograph by Adhemar Duro. The source does not publish camera or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. The circles exist only because the long exposure recorded the sky's apparent rotation.

alt: Circular star trails centred in the frame, with two diffuse bluish clouds above the centre and a dense star field at left.
